raw_response:
I am still doing wheat-maize on all 30 mu. At my age, and with only 2 people in the house and some off-farm work, I cannot make the farm too complicated. Wheat and maize are what I know best, and around here this rotation is still the safest. The money has to be spread across the whole year, so I will not push the inputs too high, but I also do not dare cut too much. If wheat or maize looks weak because I saved too much on fertilizer, that loss is bigger than the little money saved.

For wheat, I will sow in early to mid October, about the same time as most people in the village. I will use a common improved variety from the local dealer, not anything too expensive. I usually put most of the fertilizer down before sowing, with some urea held back for jointing. The extension people talk about precise rates, but on my land I still judge by last year's growth and leaf color. Since I have well water, I plan for about 3 irrigations for wheat: one after sowing if the moisture is short, one around jointing, and one around grain filling if spring is dry. For maize, the key is speed after wheat harvest. The turnaround is tight, so I will not do deep tillage. I will use the machine to harvest wheat, then quickly clear the field and sow maize. I will use hybrid seed because maize responds well, and I will give enough fertilizer to keep the stand strong, but not the highest rate because fertilizer and pumping water both cost cash. If pests are light, I will spray only when needed.
